No code conflicts: the two WPs split their files as planned (rs-speed-c: net/*; rs-speed-d: Move / legal / apply / effects / the two encoder legal-list consumers). git merged both cleanly; only RESULT.json conflicted. Nothing was dropped.

Combined speedup ~x2.0 at every setting (1x1280 x1.95, 2x1280 x2.05, 4x1280 x1.98, 1x5120 x1.99 in wall time), close to the product of the two (1.12 x 1.73 = 1.94). Mainline at 1x1280 measured 142.9 s here vs 160.5 s (rs-speed-c) / 148.4 s (rs-speed-d) in the earlier runs: machine noise between sessions; the ratio is measured side by side in the same run.

With speedup over the pre-speed mainline (speed-merge x2.00) this makes 1x1280 about x4 against the original engine. Remaining levers (from rs-speed-c / rs-speed-d notes): encode (~25%, most encodes hit the trunk cache — a board fingerprint before encoding would remove them) and apply (~27%).
Gate timing note: make test / audit-cross ran after the latency runs (not concurrently).
